A company has used infrastructure as code (IaC) to provision a set of two Amazon EC2 instances. The

instances have remained the same for several years. The company's business has grown rapidly in the past few months. In response the company's operations team has implemented an Auto Scaling group to manage the sudden increases in traffic. Company policy requires a monthly installation of security updates on all operating systems that are running. The most recent security update required a reboot. As a result, the Auto Scaling group terminated the instances and replaced them with new, unpatched instances. Which combination of steps should a solutions architect recommend to avoid a recurrence of this issue? (Choose two.)
o: Modify the Auto Scaling group by setting the Update policy to target the oldest launch configuration for replacement.
Create a new Auto Scaling group before the next patch maintenance. During the maintenance window, patch both groups and reboot the instances.

Create an Elastic Load Balancer in front of the Auto Scaling group. Configure monitoring to ensure that target group health checks return healthy after the Auto Scaling group replaces the terminated instances.
Create automation scripts to patch an AMI, update the launch configuration, and invoke an Auto Scaling instance refresh.
Create an Elastic Load Balancer in front of the Auto Scaling group. Configure termination protection on the instances.
e: To prevent Auto Scaling from launching unpatched instances when security updates require reboots: l Create a new AMI with updates: Build a new Amazon Machine Image with the latest security patches and reboots applied. This becomes the source for all new instances launched by Auto Scaling. l Update Auto Scaling group launch template: Configure the Auto Scaling group to use the new AMI with updated launch configuration/template l Implement lifecycle hooks: Add lifecycle hooks to the Auto Scaling group that pause instance termination/launch, allowing time for custom scripts to validate patch status and run updates if needed before instances are terminated l Maintain IaC: Keep infrastructure as code updated with new AMI references so future scaling uses patched versions This ensures that Auto Scaling replaces instances with pre-patched versions rather than forcing updates at runtime that trigger terminations.
x: Same scenario as A114 (keyed AD there after review). Build patched AMIs automatically, update the launch configuration and run an instance refresh (D), and target the oldest launch configuration for replacement (A). A load balancer with health monitoring (C) doesn't make new instances patched.
